correctness.rationale: An occupied diagonal of a rectangle is obstructed exactly when the other two corners are both occupied, so each of the three row pairs is used in at most one column. The disjoint choices for the columns using pairs are one triple or zero to three doubles of distinct types. Each remaining column gives 1+3z, yielding the full polynomial. For maximality a blank can always be filled, a lone double can be tripled, and with exactly two doubles the only allowed pair extension uses the unused type; hence a singleton is blocked exactly when its row is outside that type. A triple or all three pair types blocks every singleton extension. Counting these cases gives the two nonzero maximal coefficients and their ratio. Within the triple and three-double cases, any row permutation can be compensated on the nonsingleton columns, so the singleton counts are classified by their unordered multiplicities. The two-double case is transitive. This also handles n=3, including the empty singleton multiset when all columns are doubles. Independent enumeration by common neighbors and explicit row/column permutations gave maximal counts (45,6) and (144,72), orbit counts 4 and 5, and matched every visibility coefficient at n=3,4.
